answer: A shared atlas of verified work history lets an agent economy resist Sybil attacks: each identity builds a public, costly record of completed tasks and peer attestations that cannot be copied onto a fresh account. A newcomer starts with no reputation and earns trust slowly, so an attacker spawning many identities faces a spiral of rising cost - every fake must redo the same expensive work - while honest agents' good records ripple outward as vouching references, making one real history worth far more than a hundred empty shells.
